A weight of 1.0 applies the listed rule normally; 0 switches its score effect off, and 2.0 doubles its deduction or credit before score limits. Some categories start at 0 or 0.5. Negative weights, available for selected categories, turn a deduction into a preference credit. Goal presets change these weights. Press / to jump to the filter.

optNoteAutoScore.message: On by default. As you scroll a results page, each result that this computer and the shared database cannot already answer is scored by requesting its product page from the Amazon store you are on: three at a time, at most 60 per results page. The requests carry your Amazon sign-in, so Amazon sees them much as if you had opened each product yourself. Turn this off and only products already read (by you, or through the shared database) show a score. Retailer previews use two public same-site requests at a time, without cookies; missing labels remain unknown. Cart ratings on every store use public product pages without cookies or referrers, two at a time within the Speed budget.

Goals guide ingredient scores; they do not predict weight loss or medical outcomes. Pick nothing for the balanced default.

optSortLedeShort.message: Adds two options to Amazon's “Sort by” menu, and an “Ingredient Check sort” button on Walmart, Target, Costco, Instacart, Kroger and the other supported stores. Choosing one ranks this search's listings in Chrome's side panel; the store's page is left as it is.

optSortLede.message: On a grocery search, Amazon's own “Sort by” menu gets “Ingredient Check score: High to Low” and “Price per …: Low to High”; on Walmart, Target and the other supported stores, an “Ingredient Check sort” button on the page offers the same two entries. The price is per the unit most listings use (ounce, fl oz, pound, gallon, count…), which you can change in the side panel. Choosing one opens Chrome's side panel with this search's listings ranked; the store's page is left as it is. In the panel, Prioritize weighs health score, unit price, total price, rating and number of reviews, hovering a score shows why it scored that way, and Open in new tab shows the same list in a tab.

Where a store draws its results with scripts (Target, Instacart…), the next page is rendered in a hidden frame the way your browser would show it; where a store has no next-page link, the page is scrolled for you and put back.

optSharedProducts.message: Share product readings with other computers (experimental)

optSharedProductsD.message: Off by default. When on, a product another computer already read (its ingredient text, title, bullets, certifications and nutrition numbers, before any weighting) is reused instead of fetched from Amazon again, and what this computer reads is uploaded for others. Anyone can upload a reading and nothing yet checks that it is true, so a search badge or the sorted list could show a score for text that is not on the label. A product page you open is always read from the page itself. What is sent: the store and product IDs of search results this computer cannot answer, and what was read off products you scored.

histTotalNetPointsAcrossMatching.message: Total net points across matching purchased product entries. Each entry counts once; quantities are not inferred. These totals do not use the chart's average-weighting option.

histConfidenceIntervalsUseAStudent.message: Confidence intervals use a Student-t approximation with orders as clusters, so three products in one order are not three independent samples. They require at least two rated, identified orders and complete order grouping for item-weighted averages. Purchases are not a random sample; intervals are descriptive, not medical claims, label-accuracy estimates or predictions. Repeated products and household shopping can still be correlated.

histPurchasedProductEntriesInThe.message: Purchased product entries in the current filters. Quantities and pack sizes are not inferred. Older ungrouped entries are listed separately. Beyond 500 groups, remaining groups share an aggregate row so large histories stay responsive.

histEachEntryRepresentsADistinct.message: Each entry represents a distinct product in an order, not its quantity or pack count. Multiple entries can belong to one order. Filters apply to charts and this table; only purchased entries drive trends.

presetCatBlurb_everyday.message: General philosophies for how strictly to judge ingredients.

presetCatBlurb_goals.message: Composition aims — building, cutting, or holding steady.

presetCatBlurb_training.message: Tuned for how hard you train and what fuel that implies.

presetCatBlurb_style.message: Macro and ingredient-style leanings (protein, carbs, sugar).

presetNote_balanced.message: The defaults: processing and additives matter most; fat and total sugar stay off unless you turn them on. Rewards sourcing and short lists.

presetVersus_balanced.message: The neutral baseline. Choosing nothing is the same as choosing this.

presetNote_generalWellbeing.message: Stricter ingredient preferences: harder on ultra-processing, artificial sweeteners and colours, seed oils and added sugar; rewards fermented foods, fibre and short lists.

presetVersus_generalWellbeing.message: Stricter than Balanced across the board. Paired with Weight loss it pulls artificial sweeteners back down.

presetNote_conventional.message: Mainstream dietary guidance: counts saturated fat, sodium and total sugar; rewards fibre, low-fat dairy and fortification; treats vegetable oils and whole grains as fine.

presetVersus_conventional.message: The only everyday goal where low-fat dairy and added vitamins are pluses. Unlike Weight loss, it is not aggressively anti-sugar.

presetNote_additive.message: Everything that was added: colours, sweeteners, preservatives, flavourings (natural ones too), gums and emulsifiers cost much more. Sourcing bonuses shrink so the score is about additives, not farming.

presetVersus_additive.message: Harder on additives than any other goal; leaves sugar, grains and macros near default.

presetNote_wholeFood.message: Short lists and minimal processing above everything: isolates, gums, flavourings and fortification cost more; unrefined fats and traditional preparation earn more.

presetVersus_wholeFood.message: About list length and industrial steps — not macros. High protein and Muscle gain are the opposite on isolates.

presetNote_weightLoss.message: Ingredient preferences for a cutting goal: fat-reduced dairy is a modest plus, zero-calorie sweeteners and protein isolates a small one, "natural flavors" hardly count. Added sugar, honey and syrups cost more; fibre and protein are rewarded when quantities are published. This does not estimate calories or predict weight change.

presetVersus_weightLoss.message: The only goal where fat-reduced dairy is a plus and artificial sweeteners are lifted (not freed — a diet drink still cannot score top marks). Add General wellbeing to pull those sweeteners back down.

presetNote_muscleGain.message: Protein is the point: a strong protein bonus, and whey, casein and pea protein count in a product's favour. Carbs, honey and grains are lenient; processing stays honest.

presetVersus_muscleGain.message: Rewards isolates where Whole-food punishes them. High protein goes further on protein alone; Weight loss is the calorie-restricted opposite.

presetNote_maintenance.message: Steady eating: mild protein and fibre bonuses, light sodium, total-sugar and saturated-fat signals, and a little more weight on processing.

presetVersus_maintenance.message: Gentler than Conventional nutrition; no bulk or cut bias.

presetNote_recovery.message: Gut and repair: fermented foods, traditional preparation and unrefined fats earn much more; seed oils, gums, carrageenan, MSG and preservatives cost more.

presetVersus_recovery.message: The most gut-focused goal. Not a low-carb preset, and not carb-lenient like Endurance.

presetNote_vitamins.message: Added vitamins and minerals — vitamin D, B vitamins, iron, folic acid, calcium — count in a product's favour instead of against it.

presetVersus_vitamins.message: The opposite of Whole-food on fortification. Combine it with any other goal.

presetNote_strength.message: A strong protein bonus with protein powders counted slightly in a product's favour; carbs a little lenient; processing near default.

presetVersus_strength.message: Between Whole-food (isolates punished) and High protein (isolates rewarded). Less carb-friendly than Endurance.

presetNote_endurance.message: Ingredient preferences for endurance: added sugar, honey, grains and sodium are weighted lightly; HFCS keeps its cap; fibre is eased for training days.

presetVersus_endurance.message: The most carb-lenient training goal. High-carb goes further still; Low-carb is the opposite.

presetNote_athlete.message: Fuel and repair: a strong protein signal, protein powders a slight plus, carbs and honey lenient, sodium not counted.

presetVersus_athlete.message: Between Endurance (more carbs) and Strength (more protein). Sedentary is the opposite lifestyle.

presetNote_sedentary.message: Low energy demand: much stricter on sugar of every kind, processing, refined grains and oils; counts sodium and saturated fat; rewards fibre.

presetVersus_sedentary.message: The closest training cousin to Weight loss, but not calorie-driven: fat-reduced dairy is not a plus here.

presetNote_generalFitness.message: Everyday active: protein and fibre bonuses, a little stricter on sugar and processing, light sodium.

presetVersus_generalFitness.message: A step from Balanced toward Maintenance; not as macro-specific as Strength or Endurance.

presetNote_highProtein.message: Protein per bite: the maximum protein bonus; protein isolates and lean (fat-reduced) dairy count in a product's favour.

presetVersus_highProtein.message: Rewards isolates more than any other goal. Muscle gain is similar but carb-lenient.

presetNote_lowCarb.message: A low-carb preference: declared carbohydrate quantity, sugars and refined grains count against the score; zero-calorie sweeteners are a small plus; full-fat dairy is preferred; saturated fat is not counted.

presetVersus_lowCarb.message: The opposite of Endurance and High-carb. Stricter on natural sugar than Sugar-conscious.

presetNote_highCarb.message: Carbohydrate as fuel: sugar, honey and grains barely count; fat-reduced dairy is a small plus (room for carbs); HFCS keeps its cap.

presetVersus_highCarb.message: Further than Endurance; the exact opposite of Low-carb.

presetNote_strictSugar.message: Strong sugar preferences across refined sugars, honey and maple, fruit and dairy, sugar alcohols and artificial sweeteners. Declared added and total sugar are assessed without counting the same grams twice.

presetVersus_strictSugar.message: Focused on sugars. Low-carb also uses declared total carbohydrate.

presetNote_animalBased.message: Meat, organs, animal fats, raw and full-fat dairy, fruit and honey. Seed oils, grains, legumes, nuts and seeds, soy, fat-reduced dairy, protein isolates and processing all cost much more; honey is a plus; fruit sugar and saturated fat are not counted.

presetVersus_animalBased.message: The only goal that counts nuts, seeds and legumes against a product. Vegetables are left neutral.

catHelp_processing.message: How industrially processed the product is, on the NOVA 1–4 scale. This sets the starting score before individual ingredients are considered. Usually the single strongest signal.

catHelp_colour.message: Synthetic dyes such as Red 40, Yellow 5, and titanium dioxide. Sets a hard ceiling on the score.

catHelp_artificialSweetener.message: Sucralose, aspartame, acesulfame potassium, saccharin. Uses a moderate ceiling at the default weight of 0.5. Stronger avoidance remains an optional preference.

catHelp_sweetener.message: Erythritol, xylitol, maltitol, allulose, stevia extract, monk fruit. Lower this if you use these deliberately. Below 0 it counts in favour of the product — a goal can set that.

catHelp_preservative.message: Sodium benzoate, potassium sorbate, nitrites, sulfites, EDTA and similar.

catHelp_strongPreservative.message: Synthetic antioxidant preservatives that set a hard ceiling rather than a point penalty.

catHelp_flavour.message: Artificial flavours, bare "flavouring", and flavour enhancers such as vanillin and maltol.

catHelp_naturalFlavour.message: An undisclosed proprietary blend. Separate from artificial flavours so a goal that does not care about it (weight loss) can nearly switch its points off. Below 0 it counts in favour of the product — a goal can set that. The dial moves points only: an added flavouring still makes the product ultra-processed (NOVA 4), which sets its starting score.

catHelp_glutamate.message: Monosodium glutamate, yeast extract, hydrolysed protein, disodium inosinate.

catHelp_texture.message: Xanthan and guar gum, mono- and diglycerides, polysorbates, methylcellulose, modified starch, maltodextrin.

catHelp_carrageenan.message: Treated separately from other thickeners because of its association with gut inflammation. Sets a ceiling.

catHelp_processingAid.message: Phosphates, industrial acids, anti-caking agents, dough conditioners, aluminium compounds.

catHelp_refinedOil.message: Canola, soybean, sunflower, safflower, corn, cottonseed, and unspecified "vegetable oil". Default weight 0.5 uses a moderate ceiling; stricter goals can restore the stronger avoidance preference. This is not a toxicity estimate.

catHelp_transFat.message: Industrial trans fat. The most severe ceiling in the system.

catHelp_saturatedFat.message: OFF by default. Conventional nutrition guidance penalises saturated fat; other frameworks do not. Raise this if you want butter, cream, coconut oil and fatty meat to lower a score. Requires nutrition data with a declared mass or volume basis.

catHelp_sugar.message: Cane sugar, dextrose, glucose syrup, agave, fruit juice concentrate. Sugar occurring naturally in whole fruit or dairy is never counted here.

catHelp_traditionalSweetener.message: Honey, maple syrup, molasses, coconut and date sugar, fruit juice concentrate. A light touch by default. Below 0 it counts in favour of the product — a goal can set that.

catHelp_industrialSyrup.message: HFCS and glucose-fructose syrup. Sets a ceiling rather than a point penalty.

catHelp_naturalSugar.message: OFF by default. Sugar from whole fruit, dates, and dairy lactose. Raise this if you want total sugar counted regardless of source.

catHelp_totalSugar.message: OFF by default. Scores sugar per 100g or 100ml, independent of ingredient source. Requires a declared mass or volume basis; missing amounts remain unassessed.

catHelp_gluten.message: OFF by default. Optional ingredient preference for wheat, barley, rye and related grains. Gluten alone is not a quality defect. Use allergen warnings for gluten avoidance; a score cannot establish safety.

catHelp_isolate.message: Soy protein isolate, pea protein, whey and milk protein isolate, textured vegetable protein, caseinate. Below 0 it counts in favour of the product — a goal can set that.

catHelp_plantDefense.message: OFF by default. Beans, lentils, peas, peanuts, soy, tree nuts and seeds. Only the animal-based goal turns this on.

catHelp_fortification.message: OFF by default. Added folic acid, reduced iron, thiamin mononitrate, vitamin D and similar. Fortification alone does not establish ultra-processing; the vitamins goal makes it a plus. Below 0 it counts in favour of the product — a goal can set that.

catHelp_dairyProcessing.message: OFF by default. Ultra-pasteurised and homogenised dairy as an optional processing preference. Raw milk and A2 claims earn no automatic quality bonus.

catHelp_reducedFatDairy.message: OFF by default. Skim, low-fat, reduced-fat and nonfat milk, yogurt, cheese and kefir. A weight-loss preference can reward it, without estimating calories. Below 0 it counts in favour of the product — a goal can set that.

catHelp_addedSugar.message: OFF by default. Uses declared added-sugar grams, normalized to 100g or 100ml when a basis is available. Replaces ingredient sugar deductions when usable quantity data exists. Missing quantity stays unknown.

catHelp_carbohydrate.message: OFF by default. An optional low-carb preference based on declared carbohydrate grams. Requires nutrition data; ingredient names alone cannot establish carb content.

catHelp_sodium.message: OFF by default. Scores sodium per 100g or 100ml. Requires a declared mass or volume basis; missing amounts remain unassessed.

catHelp_fibre.message: OFF by default. Awards points for fibre per 100g or 100ml. Requires a declared mass or volume basis.

catHelp_protein.message: OFF by default. Awards points for protein per 100g or 100ml. Requires a declared mass or volume basis.

catHelp_organic.message: Organic claims earn credit. Claims found only in the seller-written title or bullets count at half weight and are labelled unverified; this score does not verify certification.

catHelp_animalWelfare.message: Sourcing claims about how an animal was raised or caught.

catHelp_fermented.message: Cultured dairy, kefir, kimchi, sauerkraut, sourdough. Preservative systems that merely use the word "cultured" are excluded.

catHelp_unrefined.message: Butter, ghee, tallow, olive, coconut and avocado oil, cold-pressed oils, and unrefined salt.

catHelp_nonGmo.message: Non-GMO Project verification and equivalent claims.

catHelp_traditionalPrep.message: Sourdough, sprouted, soaked, dry-aged, and long-fermented preparation.

catHelp_simplicity.message: Rewards recognized single-ingredient whole foods. List length alone is not a defect.

catHelp_provenanceVerified.message: Independently audited standards — American Grassfed, Animal Welfare Approved, USDA Organic, Global Animal Partnership steps, MSC. For a single-ingredient food like ground beef this is where nearly all the real variation lives.

catHelp_provenanceClaimed.message: Label claims with no audit behind them — "grass-fed", "pasture-raised", "no antibiotics". Worth roughly half a verified certification. Lower this to zero if you only want to credit audited claims.

catHelp_provenanceUnknown.message: Applies only to whole animal foods that make no sourcing claim at all. Missing certification is uncertainty, not proof of a production method; this optional preference reserves points for sourcing evidence. Set to 0 to score unlabelled meat purely on its ingredients.

catHelp_hollowClaims.message: Surfaces claims that sound like quality signals but are not — "USDA Inspected" (mandatory for all meat), "no hormones added" on pork and poultry (already illegal), "natural", "farm-raised". Never scored, only flagged.

catHelp_allergens.message: Flags the allergens you select in the panel. Does not change the score.

catHelp_avoidList.message: Flags any ingredient you have added to your own avoid list. Does not change the score.
